A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedGVI research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic outlier experiments and evaluations on CoverType, MNIST, and Fashion-MNIST, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds architecture controls, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, convergence comparisons, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the client/server updates in Equations 3–7 are retained. The additional loss and kernel formulas document existing components, while the new experiments vary existing architecture and hyperparameter choices.

E1.justification: All datasets and tasks are retained. Fashion-MNIST adds an explicitly evaluated 10% random-label-contamination condition to the earlier 0%, 20%, and 40% conditions, as documented in v1 Appendix C.3.2 and v2 Appendix D.3.2.

E2.justification: The Fashion-MNIST comparison expands from PVI versus FedGVI variants in v1 Figure 2 to include FedAvg, FedPA, and beta-PredBayes in v2 Tables 2 and 6. These methods already participated in the MNIST comparison; the other principal comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds comparisons controlling network architecture across methods using one 200-neuron layer versus two 100-neuron layers (Table 3). It also introduces three-client learning-rate experiments, five-client MNIST sensitivity experiments, and error-versus-per-client-wall-clock evaluation. These substantially expand evaluation controls and procedures while retaining the original Table 1 setting.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained influence and contamination analyses, v2 adds a joint loss/divergence parameter ablation (Figure 6), architecture controls, learning-rate sensitivity, and small loss-parameter perturbations (Tables 3–5). Figures 10–12 examine convergence stability and computational overhead, addressing whether gains depend on architecture, tuning, or additional computation.

E5.justification: Fashion-MNIST gains explicit plus/minus uncertainty reporting in v2 Tables 2 and 6, whereas v1 Figure 2 showed accuracy curves without uncertainty bars. The existing MNIST standard deviations, five-run information, and CoverType split counts are retained; no increase in repetitions or new significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: MNIST Table 1 is numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantial architecture, tuning, convergence, and timing results and expands and revises Fashion-MNIST results. For example, new Table 3 reports 96.77 ± 0.10% for combined FedGVI versus 96.64 ± 0.07% for FedAvg in the two-hidden-layer, ten-client setting. These are newly reported controlled comparisons.

T1.justification: V2 restores beta in Equation 2's normalizing constant and specifies beta = 1 for recovering ordinary Bayes. It adds the convexity/global-optimality statement in Remark 4.5 and makes Proposition 4.4 explicitly local. The corresponding Appendix B proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V1's abstract claims provable robustness to both prior and likelihood misspecification. V2 retains robustness to both but specifically limits its provable-robustness claim to likelihood misspecification. The principal framework, generalization, cavity-distribution, conjugacy, and predictive-performance contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds the qualification that robust losses can underperform under correct likelihood specification and explicitly identifies proving prior robustness as an open problem. It also interprets the new sensitivity and runtime evidence, conjectures that contamination exacerbates baseline instability, and discusses challenges in extending FedGVI to personalized and hierarchical FL.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised future code release with an explicit repository pointer. Appendix D substantially expands documentation with loss, kernel, and divergence formulas and newly specifies 99 observations plus one outlier and convergence-based execution for the retained influence experiment. Some added details contain inconsistencies, including the Alpha-Renyi formula's sign relative to Section 3.3.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning around personalized and hierarchical Bayesian FL and adds references including Kim and Hospedales, Hassan et al. (2023), Swaroop et al., and Yonekura and Sugasawa. Section 4.7 also attributes the robust losses to GVI instead of FedGVI. The central relationship to PVI and generalized inference remains.

P1.justification: The main section order and most methodological and proof prose are retained. V2 rewrites the notation setup, expands explanatory passages, completes unfinished appendix prose, and introduces a contextual Appendix C while moving the experimental appendix to D. These are localized revisions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds relationship diagrams, a parameter heatmap, architecture and sensitivity tables, and convergence/runtime plots. The Fashion-MNIST plot becomes expanded tables, with Table 6 redisplaying Table 2 at higher precision. Retained experimental figures are repositioned closer to their corresponding discussions, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: V1's principal comparison used different network depths across methods; v2's Table 3 directly addresses that confound. The sensitivity, convergence, and runtime analyses substantially strengthen practical validation, while the narrowed provability claim improves scientific precision. Expanded documentation also helps reproducibility. Ambiguous labels in Tables 4–5 and the Appendix D Alpha-Renyi sign inconsistency detract from precision, but these localized defects do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support and claim calibration.
